entries.text: Catch-up push: this morning's Wiggle Friends Christmas Set and the Toy Memory game, plus a Toy Memory YouTube Short, are now on the public website. The earlier push from the workshop had been refused, so the site was a day behind.

New game in the playground: Toy Memory. Every card hides one of our real toy friends from the model library; tap two cards to peek, and matching twins stay up and cheer. Six cards first, then eight, then twelve, no fail screen: after three misses in a row a pair wiggles as a hint. It reads the toy library, so every new figure joins the deck by itself. Tested on a phone-size screen in English and Vietnamese with zero page errors. Today's Wiggle Friends are print-in-place toys rather than a figure, so the game library itself is unchanged. Note: this morning's copy to the public website could not be pushed (the code host refused access from the workshop), so the website shows today's set and game once the next push goes through.

New print-in-place set for the Christmas stockings: Wiggle Friends, four 10 cm articulated minis of our own design (a reindeer with antlers and a red nose, a snowman with a carrot nose and scarf, a penguin and a gingerbread friend with icing and gumdrops). Each prints in one piece on the same captured double-cone pins as the Rainbow Wiggle Snake: 6 segments on 5 pins, 45-degree overhangs only, 0.55 mm clearance. Why now: an Etsy pack of 3D-printed articulating animals has 640 five-star reviews at 9.99 USD, small articulated toys are classic stocking stuffers, and Christmas buyers start searching in November. Checks: every friend is watertight with 0 bad edges and exactly 6 separate shells (24 of 24, no fused joint); all 13 colour parts of the AMS 3MF are closed too. The download is one colour-split 3MF that also prints in a single colour. Small parts: not for children under 3.

New game in the playground: Magic Printer. One of our real 3D toys is cut into layers, the way a 3D printer builds it; tap the layers from the bottom up and the little printer stacks them until the toy hops and spins. Three layers at first, then four and five, six toys a game, no fail screen: after two wrong taps the right layer bounces as a hint. It reads the toy library, so every new figure joins it by itself. Tested on a phone-size screen in English and Vietnamese with zero page errors. Today's snake is a print-in-place toy rather than a figure, so the game library itself is unchanged. Note: this morning's copy to the public website could not be pushed (the code host refused access from the workshop), so the website shows these updates once the next push goes through.

New print-in-place toy: the Rainbow Wiggle Snake, a 21 cm articulated snake of our own design that prints in one piece and slithers straight off the bed. Thirteen rainbow segments ride on twelve captured double-cone pins, so every overhang is 45 degrees, nothing bridges and each joint swings about 25 degrees with 0.55 mm clearance. Why now: articulated snakes are one of the steadiest sellers in 3D-printed toys (about 2,200 sold a month for one Amazon listing per Accio, and a flexi ball python on Etsy has 399 five-star reviews), and small wiggle toys are classic stocking stuffers for the weeks before Christmas. Checks: watertight, 0 bad edges, 13 separate shells as designed (no fused joints), 210 x 19 x 12 mm. The download has one STL plus a 3MF split into six colour groups for AMS printers. Small parts: not for children under 3.

New game in the playground: Whose Shadow? One of our real 3D toys turns slowly as a dark shadow on a little stage; tap the friend it belongs to and the lights come on. Eight rounds, three picture choices at first and then four, no fail screen: after two wrong taps the right friend wiggles as a hint. Tested on a phone-size screen with zero page errors, in English and Vietnamese. The new Gingerbread Buddy also joined Hide and Seek and Toy Bowling.

New figure for the Christmas season: the Gingerbread Buddy, a chubby gingerbread cookie friend of our own design with white icing trim, three gumdrop buttons and a knitted scarf, sculpted in Sculpt Studio v2. Why now: Google Trends interest in gingerbread Christmas ornaments climbed from 9 in October to a peak of 74 in December last year (Accio trend report), and a mini gingerbread figure set on MakerWorld has 64 comments and ratings, so demand should build over the next 4-8 weeks. The body is one solid piece (watertight, 0 bad edges, one shell, 62 x 35 x 70 mm) and all five colour parts passed the closed-surface check. It also joins Hide and Seek and Toy Bowling as a new toy.

Sharper 3D previews for the sculpted figures: the viewer now loads a clean preview mesh per colour with smooth shading, colour borders are softened, and the first four animals were re-sculpted at 160-cubed resolution. Print files are unchanged in shape and still pass the closed-surface check.

Four more figures sculpted in Sculpt Studio v2 at 160-cubed resolution: a fox cub, a grinning frog, an axolotl and a tabby kitten, all original designs shaped with the same brushes the app offers (clay blobs, Pinch for ear tips, Dam Standard for smiles, Smooth along every limb). While making them we found and fixed a brush bug that left faint ridges where clay blobs overlapped, and re-sculpted the first four animals with the fix. All eight bodies and every colour part passed the closed-surface check.

New figure set made with our own Sculpt Studio, the in-browser clay app that just launched: a chick, a bunny, a bear cub and a penguin, all original designs. Each comes as one solid STL plus a colour-split 3MF where the colour regions tile the body exactly, so a multi-colour print has no gaps and no loose parts. All four bodies and every colour part passed the closed-surface check after a position-weld test, the same way slicers read them.

Batch 2 is live, picked from market research instead of guesswork. Gridfinity storage is searched about 90,000 times a month and grew 76% in two years, so a free Gridfinity starter set brings people in. Christmas decor is the strongest seasonal seller on Etsy from November, so a four-piece flat ornament set is today's featured paid model. Print-in-place flexi animals sell year-round; the Flexi Fishbone lands just before Halloween. An AirTag collar holder covers the pet-accessory demand. All four passed the closed-surface check; the fishbone has eight separate shells, one per moving segment, so no joint is fused.
Shop opened with six printable models across four lines: two desk organizers, a print-in-place fidget, two decor pieces and a four-part multi-colour whale.
Every file is checked before it is listed: closed surfaces, one shell per part, size and volume recorded. Six of six passed with zero open edges.
Payments are not connected yet. Buy and membership buttons walk through the checkout in demo mode, and free models download for real.
Next drop is scheduled for tomorrow at 09:00 (Vietnam time). The rotation runs functional, print-in-place, decor, then figure, so every line gets a new model each week.
